nodes.label: CDKL5 deficiency disorder
nodes.lay_summary: A rare genetic condition caused by changes in the CDKL5 gene, usually beginning with seizures in the first months of life.

nodes.label: Rett syndrome

connections.why_connected: Children with CDD and children with Rett syndrome can share several features, such as seizures, low muscle tone and repetitive hand movements.
connections.key_difference: Seizures in CDD usually start in the first months of life; Rett more often follows a period of typical early development and then regression.

connections.why_connected: CDD was once described as a form of Rett syndrome, so the two communities share research history.
connections.key_difference: Current literature (to be retrieved) treats CDD as its own disorder. Shared history is not the same as shared biology.

connections.why_connected: An AI-generated hypothesis suggests both genes may affect how brain connections (synapses) develop.
connections.key_difference: The genes do different jobs (CDKL5 is an enzyme; MeCP2 regulates other genes). A shared downstream effect is unproven.

connections.why_connected: FOXG1 syndrome is another neurodevelopmental condition with some overlapping features.
connections.key_difference: Different gene and different typical features; overlap score has not been computed yet.

opportunities.headline: Natural-history protocol from the Rett syndrome community
why_it_may_transfer: Overlapping clinical features (seizures, low muscle tone, hand movements) mean some visit assessments may already fit CDD.
Shared research history means investigators may already know both conditions.
what_differs: Age at onset: CDD seizures usually begin in early infancy; a Rett schedule may start too late to capture this.
Different gene and protein function (kinase vs. gene regulator).
Seizure burden is typically central in CDD and may need heavier measurement.
what_is_uncertain: Whether CDD participants were ever eligible for or enrolled in this study (not yet checked).
Whether the protocol is shareable and under what terms.
requires_expert_validation: Would the visit schedule and assessments capture the earliest CDD milestones?
Which protocol elements would need to change for a seizure-dominant, early-onset population?

next_actions.label: Pull the study's registry record and read its eligibility and visit schedule
Ask the International Rett Syndrome Foundation who coordinates the study and whether the protocol can be shared
Bring the 'what differs' list to your scientific advisory board before adapting anything

opportunities.headline: Outcome measures developed for Rett syndrome
why_it_may_transfer: Measures of motor, hand-use and communication skills target features that partly overlap with CDD.
what_differs: CDD commonly involves visual impairment and early seizures that Rett instruments may not capture.
The typical regression pattern differs between the two conditions.
what_is_uncertain: Whether these instruments have ever been validated in CDD.
Whether CDD-specific measures already exist that should be preferred (check first).
requires_expert_validation: Are these measures psychometrically valid in CDD, or would they need re-validation?

next_actions.label: List the instruments from the Rett study record side by side with any CDD-specific measures
Ask study investigators whether the instruments were tried in CDD participants
